articles.summary: Machine translation tests masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) because every source token must be rendered faithfully, while fixed canvas decoding must choose target length before denoising. articles.title: Best Practice Critic Optimization

A reliable critic could instead estimate token-level advantages from one response, but standard critic-based training recipes are often unstable. articles.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) and on-policy distillation (OPD) have become two widely adopted paradigms for post-training large language models. articles.summary: Outcome-supervised search agents learn when and how to retrieve evidence, but terminal rewards neither localize intermediate errors nor redirect an ongoing trajectory before those errors compound. articles.title: LongRCA Bench: Diagnosing Responsible Roles and Root Causes in Long-Horizon Agent Failures
articles.summary: When a long-horizon agent execution fails, outcome-level evaluation reveals the unsuccessful result but not where the decisive error entered the trajectory. Developers must then inspect the full execution to identify the responsible role and localize the earliest decisive root-cause step. articles.title: The Mask Is Not the Model: Auditing Prefix Invariance in Attention, State-Space, and Hybrid Sequence Models
articles.summary: We formalize prefix invariance: representations at position t must not depend on future inputs. We give a lightweight audit, two forward passes, no training or gradients, that localizes exactly where causality breaks. Attention-mask inspection is incomplete: leaks can occur via scans or normalization despite correct masks. Across 192 injected-fault trials on eight checkpoints, mask inspection found none, while our audit localized all 192/192, also finding a defect in Zamba2 and Nemotron-H.

articles.summary: Large language models are increasingly expected to execute complex workflows whose success depends on maintaining interdependent constraints and producing artifacts that satisfy strict end-to-end verification. articles.title: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out
articles.summary: Autonomous research systems are increasingly capable of executing long research workflows, yet automation alone does not ensure that the resulting process remains scientifically grounded. articles.title: Quantization-Aware Healing: A Practical Recipe for Recovering Compressed, 4-Bit LLMs
articles.summary: Serving large language models cheaply increasingly means shipping models that are both structurally compressed to a fraction of their parameters and quantized to 4 bits. Together these steps degrade reasoning, mathematics, coding, and long-context behavior enough to require a recovery, or healing, stage before deployment. The default recipe, quantization-aware training (QAT), re-fits the compressed, quantized model to hard labels; in our pipeline it converged slowly and collapsed past its peak.

articles.title: EXPL-FR: Explaining Face Recognition Models via Vision-Language Alignment

articles.summary: User representation learning in real-world industrial scenarios is commonly scaled by increasing user amount, behavioral sequence length and model size. articles.summary: With the rapid progress of diffusion models and large-scale video generation, generative world models are increasingly expected to replace traditional simulators, including physics engines, game engines, and reinforcement-learning environments. articles.summary: Policy optimization (PO) for Large Language Models faces a stability--exploration trade-off, currently mediated by an action-side Policy-KL regularizer. This puts practitioners in a double bind: keeping Policy-KL constrains response behavior and consumes the action-side exploration budget, while dropping it leaves the optimization without an explicit drift control. articles.summary: We present EchoWM, an omnimodal world model for enterable generative media that responds to continuous navigation while jointly generating 720p video, environmental sound, music and speech. articles.summary: Recent agent benchmarks increasingly ground evaluation in executable environments, from code repair to web navigation, app APIs, and function calling. articles.summary: Search-augmented LLMs increasingly mediate everyday consumer recommendations by retrieving live web content. This creates a new risk: LLM recommenders may consume web content that Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) operators have polluted to mislead them. articles.title: Block3D: Efficient Text-to-3D Generation via Block-Wise Diffusion
articles.summary: While text-to-3D generation has advanced rapidly, achieving high geometric fidelity at low inference cost remains challenging. articles.title: MobilePA-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Planner Agents on Complex Real-World Tasks
articles.summary: As on-device LLM agents evolve into personal copilots, the mobile operating system has become a key testbed for this paradigm, making rigorous capability evaluation essential. articles.title: Task-CoEvolve: Efficient Harness Optimization via Adaptive Validation Task Selection
articles.summary: We present a novel approach to efficient LLM harness optimization through adaptive validation task selection. articles.title: ARC: Fair Relative Advantage Comparison in Open-Ended Real-World Interaction
articles.summary: Open-ended real-world interaction admits multiple valid behaviors: an agent may answer directly, ask for clarification, provide progress updates, or confirm before acting. articles.title: GameXpert-Bench: How Far Are Coding Agents from Expert Game Development?
articles.summary: Recent large language models (LLMs) can operate as coding agents that build complete games from natural language requests. articles.summary: Existing image editing frameworks predominantly follow the training paradigm of text-to-image diffusion models. articles.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
articles.summary: An interactive world model must follow the user's actions, remember the places it has shown, and stream in real time. articles.title: TileMix: Tile-Centric Mixed-Precision Attention for LLM Inference Acceleration

articles.title: RISE: Adaptive Imagination for World Action Models
articles.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) improve planning by incorporating future world evolution into action generation, yet existing methods allocate a fixed imagination budget to every scene. articles.summary: E-commerce live streaming requires omni-modal understanding of noisy, temporally extended streams, where product facts are distributed across speech, video frames, product images, overlaid text, and user queries.
